paragraphs: Amazon has held talks about letting Meta’s Muse AI agent shop on its online marketplace, according to a report from Fortune. The discussions, which could end Amazon’s block on Muse, reportedly center on the kinds of products the AI agent recommends and the potential impact on the ecommerce giant’s advertising revenue.

As reported by Fortune, Amazon is concerned that it could lose advertising revenue by allowing Muse on its site, since it depends on actual humans seeing ads across its online marketplace. It’s also reportedly worried about the quality of the product search results that Muse will present to users, as well as whether the AI agent will affect Amazon’s relationship with customers. Neither Amazon nor Meta immediately responded to The Verge’s request for comment.

Though some online retailers, such as Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, and Sephora, have opened their digital doors to AI agents like Muse, Amazon has been more hesitant. Amazon also blocked Perplexity’s AI agent from shopping on its site, and has instead focused on promoting its own Alexa for Shopping assistant, which customers can now text to shop on their behalf.

news.title_en: Behind Binance Hack, a Reckoning Over Who Controls Crypto

inline_images.caption: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino/Bloomberg

news.author: Bloomberg
news.content_snippet:
As North Korean cyberthieves were funneling billions out of Binance last month, the world’s largest crypto exchange looked to two other companies to help stop the bleeding: Tether and Circle.

The duo, which issue cryptocurrencies that mimic the US dollar, reacted unusually quickly to freeze accounts hackers were using to move their haul around. It was a sign of the seriousness of the hack, the industry’s maturation, and the most public showcasing yet of the near-total control Tether and Circle
news.summary_en: During the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $1.5 billion in USDT and $1.1 billion in USDC within 30 minutes, respectively. This action marks a significant shift as the two issuers utilized centralized control over their smart contracts to execute immediate asset blocks upon requests from government authorities and the affected exchange.
paragraphs: As North Korean cyberthieves were funneling billions out of Binance last month, the world’s largest crypto exchange looked to two other companies to help stop the bleeding: Tether and Circle.

The duo, which issue cryptocurrencies that mimic the US dollar, reacted unusually quickly to freeze accounts hackers were using to move their haul around. It was a sign of the seriousness of the hack, the industry’s maturation, and the most public showcasing yet of the near-total control Tether and Circle exert over the tokens they created. They dominate the market, with their two main stablecoins together representing 86% of all in circulation.

As the $6.3 billion Binance hack was unfolding, Tether froze more than $1.5 billion of its USDT coin in 30 minutes, while Circle froze $1.1 billion of its USDC. Their swift actions – prompted by requests from Binance as well as the US government — became a tourniquet for what would otherwise have been a much more severe and expensive heist.

Until now, Tether and Circle have largely had different approaches to freezing, which essentially means blocking movement to and from specific addresses on blockchain networks that shift crypto around.

Tether has been criticized for not having a consistent modus operandi, sometimes allowing tokens to slide away unimpeded and other times seizing them indefinitely. It sometimes charges a fee to eventually return them, according to customers who described their experiences. Meanwhile, Circle’s philosophy until recently had been to only act after receiving a court order, a method so structured and time-consuming that the judge’s decision could be irrelevant by the time it came.

But during the Binance cybertheft, both companies acted almost immediately — in a fashion Circle referred to as “machine speed.” Luckily for Binance, which owns a stake in Circle, the company took a different tack than in some prior hacking episodes. Back in May, it also changed a policy stated on its website to only require a legal order from a government authority rather than from a court.
A spokesperson said this language change reflected “longstanding practice.”

Binance also temporarily halted withdrawals and fully restored stolen assets to customers’ accounts at its own expense, marking a relative success for crypto investors who might otherwise be suffering losses or left in limbo. Yet the speed of the Binance response stands in contrast to the experience of victims of earlier hacks, some of whom have spent years trying to recover frozen funds.

Take Bittok Technology Pte. Ltd., a small Singaporean crypto exchange that lost $50 million to hackers in June 2020. Tether decided to freeze some of the assets. But after more than five years, none of Bittok’s USDT had been returned after a circuitous path through attorney wrangling.

Along the way, a lawyer representing Tether advised the entity that acquired Bittok about a 20% “reissuance fee” on whatever was returned, according to emails reviewed by Bloomberg News. It’s not the only time Tether has done so: in several instances, victims only received their stolen USDT in chunks over time, with the same kind of fee, according to people involved who did not want to be identified because the negotiations were private.

Berlin-based Valentyn Golyshenko pleaded for help online for months from Tether, regulators and politicians after getting caught in a $75,000 scam, according to his social-media posts. In his telling, requests to freeze funds were rejected, and ultimately the wallet holding his pilfered crypto was drained to zero. Tether Chief Executive Officer Paolo Ardoino appears to have blocked him, and Golyshenko recently made his X account private.
In Circle’s case, the company has mostly been accused of being too prescriptive.

prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]

2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；

4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。

prompts.code_snippet:
# 1. 启动项目自动化分析与上下文轻量修剪 (避免上下文爆炸)
claude --compact

# 2. 静默批量执行单元测试与自动修复任务 (CI/CD 友好模式)
claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

# 3. 指定单文件隔离审查模式 (限制仅允许读取特定子目录)
claude --allowed-tools "View,Replace,RunCommand" \
  --dangerously-skip-permissions false \
  -p "Audit security vulnerabilities in auth.py and output remediation report."

# 4. 自动化提交并生成符合 Conventional Commits 规范的 Commit 信息
claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

"""
